seo.title: AI-Driven Conversion Optimization Platform — Case Study
seo.description: How I re-architected a tightly coupled monorepo into independently deployable applications and cut build cycles by 15-20%.

sections.title: A monorepo where nothing could ship alone.

items.src: I joined a platform where a change in one app could break another without warning. The monorepo had grown organically, with shared code, apps, and data layers tangled together. Build times climbed, deployments were monolithic, and no team could ship on its own schedule.

src: Every deploy shipped the entire monorepo, whether or not it changed.
Shared UI and data logic had no clear boundary from app code.
Routing instability under Next.js App Router surfaced in production.

items.src: Separate apps, shared UI, and data layers

I split the monorepo into distinct applications, a shared UI package, and a shared data layer with Turborepo managing the build graph. Backend APIs and core database workflows were rebuilt with NestJS, Express, and Prisma, replacing logic that had been scattered across app-level code.

src.title: Independent deploys over one big release
src.desc: Splitting the build graph meant every app could ship on its own schedule instead of waiting on a single monolithic release train.

src.title: Pages Router over App Router
src.desc: App Router's routing behavior was unstable for this codebase's data-fetching patterns at the time. I migrated back to Pages Router for ecosystem compatibility and predictable routing.

items.src: Moving from App Router to Pages Router mid-project meant every route needed a working equivalent before the old one could be retired. I migrated route groups incrementally behind feature checks, verifying each one in production before removing the old path.
Keeping the build graph fast as apps split

Splitting one app into several risked making local builds slower, not faster, if the dependency graph wasn't disciplined. I used Turborepo's caching and explicit package boundaries so only the apps affected by a change rebuilt.

src.label: Faster build cycles after the re-architecture
Of apps deployable independently of one another
Production incidents during the routing migration

items.src: Boundaries are a build decision before they're a code decision.

The hardest part of this rebuild wasn't writing new code, it was deciding where one app's responsibility ended and another's began. Once those boundaries were explicit in the build graph, the code that respected them followed naturally.
